🌐 Web query:

`Does functools.cached_property allow direct instance attribute assignment to override the cached value, unlike property?`

💡 Result:

Yes, functools.cached_property allows direct instance attribute assignment to override the cached value, which is a key difference from the built-in property decorator [1][2]. Unlike property, which is a data descriptor that typically blocks attribute writes unless a setter is explicitly defined, cached_property is a non-data descriptor [3][1][2]. When accessed, a cached_property computes its value once and writes it directly to the instance's dict under the same name as the property [1][2]. Because the value is stored as a normal instance attribute, subsequent reads or writes to that attribute bypass the cached_property method entirely, effectively allowing you to manually override the cached value or set it directly [1][4][2]. Additionally, you can clear the cached value by deleting the attribute using del, which will cause the cached_property to recompute the value upon the next access [1][4][2].
